items.title: Maine Blood Donation Day - September 4 — Governor of Maine — Official Documents (Executive Orders)
items.content_text:
WHEREAS
, the State of Maine is committed to ensuring the safety and security of all those living in and visiting our state; and
WHEREAS
, a sufficient blood supply is a public health issue both locally and nationally, and our hospitals and medical centers need a readily available supply for our residents and visitors; and
WHEREAS
, one blood donation can help save more than one life, and although most of the U.S. population is eligible to donate blood, only about 3 percent actually do; and
WHEREAS
, Maine is home to many organizations committed to raising awareness about the importance of blood donation, including the American Red Cross; and
WHEREAS
, Maine Blood Donation Day effectively serves to remind us that we need to constantly replenish our blood supply through donation and community awareness;
NOW THEREFORE
, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 4th, 2026 as
Maine Blood Donation Day
throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all Maine people to support our local blood drives as saving lives and protecting our residents is our primary goal.
In testimony whereof, I have caused
the Great Seal of the State to be
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my
hand at Augusta this seventeenth day
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

items.title: National Clean Energy Week - September 15 through 19 — Governor of Maine — Official Documents (Executive Orders)

Direct Support Professionals Recognition Week
throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize these individuals who provide vital support and care for older adults, people with intellectual disabilities, autism spectrum disorder and other related conditions and help them live full and meaningful lives in their community.

items.title: US Labor Department finds Wisconsin food manufacturer repeatedly exposed workers to safety hazards following 2 incidents, 3 fatalities — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
items.content_text: JANESVILLE, WI – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Wisconsin-based food products manufacturer after two incidents involving industrial kettles releasing hot steam and liquid, causing three worker deaths and two serious injuries.Investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to the first incident on Feb. 12, 2026, at IPMF LLC, operating as NaturPak. The incident involved the lid of an industrial kettle unexpectedly opening after a clogged vent line led to pressure building up, and then releasing steam, liquid, and organic material onto two employees nearby. One of the employees was also struck by an object and suffered a concussion. Both employees were hospitalized, and one later passed away because of complications from their injuries. A month later, OSHA investigators responded to another incident involving multiple worker hospitalizations on March 18, when a kettle lid opened while under pressure releasing steam, hot liquid, and organic material, burning three workers. Two workers were fatally injured and another hospitalized. OSHA issued the employer one serious citation for the design and usage of kettles leading to pressure and thermal burn hazards; a repeat citation for exposing workers to falls to lower levels; and an other-than-serious citation for failing to notify employees working adjacent to permit-required confined spaces.OSHA also issued serious citations for exposing workers to thermal hazards without quick access to emergency water. The employer also received citations for exposing workers to falls into the kettles and for failure to assess personal protective equipment for thermal risks. Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

items.content_html: WASHINGTON – The United States today announced the successful resolution of the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism matter at the Grupo Yazaki, S.A. de C.V. facility located in Leon, Guanajuato, Mexico. The United States has resumed liquidation of tariffs on goods from the Yazaki facility, which manufactures automotive components, wire harnesses, and electronic components. The resolution represents real progress in protecting American workers’ ability to compete in trade, requiring Mexican manufacturers to comply with Mexican law and the provisions of the USMCA. It is another win for the Trump Administration, whose America First approach puts American workers first by ensuring auto parts suppliers in other countries do not undermine worker protections to gain an unfair trade advantage or attract investment. The Department of Labor’s Bureau of International Labor Affairs and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative facilitated a resolution with the Government of Mexico to remediate workers’ claims at Yazaki.Actions taken by Yazaki to address the matter include:Issuing a neutrality statement and company guidelines related to freedom of association and collective bargaining;Adopting a policy to respect the rights of minority unions that do not hold ownership of the collective bargaining agreement; andSigning a letter of commitment to deliver the neutrality statement and company guidelines to workers, train workers on the same, provide space for Mexico’s Secretariat of Labor and Social Welfare to train workers on freedom of association and collective bargaining, and publish and disseminate to workers the company’s minority union policy.Actions taken by Mexico to address the matter include: Delivering in-person trainings for all company personnel on freedom of association and collective bargaining; andMonitoring the facility and engaging with the workers and the company throughout its review period.Based on these measures, the United States Trade Representative directed the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility. Background The United States‑Mexico‑Canada Agreement’s innovative enforcement tool, the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism, enables the U.S. government to act quickly and directly at the facility level when workers in Mexico are denied the rights of freedom of association and collective bargaining. The United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement that coordinates U.S. efforts related to enforcement actions on USMCA labor obligations, including the RRM. On October 20, 2025, the ILC received an RRM petition from Sindicato Independiente Nacional de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de la Industria Automotriz, a Mexican independent union. The petition alleges that Yazaki and an incumbent union at the facility have violated workers’ rights by interfering in employees’ union activity and retaliating against workers because of their attempts to organize an independent union at the facility. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms. As a result, on November 19, 2025, the United States Trade Representative submitted a request to Mexico to review the matter. Mexico accepted the request, conducted an investigation, and worked with Yazaki to implement measures aimed at safeguarding freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. The United States has reviewed the matter and concluded the situation to have been remediated.As a result of the above actions taken by Yazaki and Mexico to resolve the action, the United States agrees that there is no ongoing denial of rights. Ambassador Greer’s letter directing the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility is available here. Learn more about the department’s work to make global competition fair for American workers.

The Division of Policy posts all proposed and recently adopted rules on MaineCare’s Policy and Rules webpage. This website keeps the rules on file until they are finalized and until the Secretary of State website is updated to reflect the changes. The MaineCare Benefits Manual is available on-line at the Secretary of State’s website.

Notice of Agency Rule-making Proposal

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) [Ch. I, Sec. 1, General Administrative Policies and Procedures]

TYPE OF RULE: Routine Technical

PROPOSAL FILING NUMBER: 2026-P195

BRIEF SUMMARY: This rulemaking is proposed via two, simultaneous private citizen petitions submitted to the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) on June 23, 2026, to adopt or modify a rule. The petitioners provided the specific rule changes proposed here as part of their petitions. Under 5 M.R.S. § 8055, the Department of Health and Human Services (Department) is required to initiate rulemaking proceedings on the petitioners’ proposals within 60 days because each petition was signed by 150 or more registered voters. Because the Department may only propose one set of amendments to a rule at any given time, this rulemaking combines the two petitioned rule amendments into a single rulemaking.

The proposed rule would amend Chapter I, Section 1 of the MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) to require the Department to conduct in-person, On-Site Reviews and On-Site Inspections of MaineCare provider business or service locations and authorize the Department to impose sanctions when a provider fails to permit access to the Department for such On-Site Visit, Review, or Inspection. The proposed rule would require the Department to suspend a MaineCare provider’s claims payments, under defined criteria, and to escrow withheld payments upon notice of improper payment with the issuance of a Payment Suspension and Escrow Order (PSEO). The rule proposes to escrow such suspended and hold payments until a final determination is made as to the existence and amount of any improper payment. The petitioners also propose that the Department require providers under payment suspension to continue to deliver medically necessary covered services to current MaineCare members.

The petitioners also propose that the Department work with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to obtain any necessary approvals to amend the State Plan to enact these reforms.

PUBLIC HEARING: The Department will hold a combined in-person and remote (via Zoom) public hearing.

Location: State Office Building, Conference Rooms A and B, 109 Capitol Street, Augusta, ME

Zoom Meeting Link: https://mainestate.zoom.us/j/82472273200

FRIENDS OF EASTERN BAY 
 
v. 
 
DEPARTMENT OF MARINE RESOURCES et al. 
 
 
DOUGLAS, J. 
[¶1]  In October 2024 , the Commissioner of the Maine Department of 
Marine Resources granted Acadia Aqua Farms ’ application for a twenty-year 
aquaculture lease of 19.71 acres in the coastal waters of Eastern Bay off Mount 
Desert Island for the cultivation of blue mussels and other shellfish.  Friends of 
Eastern Bay, one of the intervenors in the proceeding before the Department, 
appeals from a judgment  entered in the Business and Consumer Docket  
(McKeon, J. ) affirming  the Commissioner’s decision granting Acadia’s  
application for the lease.  We affirm the judgment. 
 2 
I.  BACKGROUND 
 [¶2]  In November 2019 , Acadia applied for a twenty -year standard 
aquaculture lease1 of 48.11 acres of coastal water in Eastern Bay, located in an 
area approximately 1,000 feet from shore southwest of Googins Ledge in the 
town of Bar Harbor.  Acadia proposed to culture blue mussels using a floating 
pipe system at the water’s surface with nets hanging down in the water column 
to collect blue mussel seed.  The mussel seed would be  harvested using 
specially designed machiner y that is lowered over the collecti on netting  to 
remove the seed with a brushing mechanism.  The harvesting machine uses a 
hydraulic system to then pump the seed  into a seventy -four-foot transport 
vessel.   
[¶3]  Acadia intends to use the harvesting machine seasonally, from May 
to October, for up to a total of three weeks during those months.  W hen not in 
use, the machine would be stored on a twenty-foot-by-twenty-foot floating raft 
permanently moored within the lease sit e.  During the off -season, the 
harvesting machine may  be removed from the lease site.

Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Aug 17, 2026

A refreshed and upgraded MIHMS is coming in mid October 2026. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS), in partnership with Gainwell Technologies, is launching an upgraded MIHMS, to bring enhanced security, improved usability, and a more modern experience to better support your day-to-day work.

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality.

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal.

Trading Partners Preparation

This message is part of a series about changes to how trading partners will access the new portal and what you must do now to prepare for these changes.

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account.

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.

Activity/Change

Your Action

Why it Matters

What’s Next?

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal.

 

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts.

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage.

 

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users.

 

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need to re-invite all other active users. More Admin (R7) users mean less re-invitation work for each user.

 

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure.

 

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

In the new portal, your username will be your email address.

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address.

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address.

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work.

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live.

 

Admin (R7) will be able to choose from ~40 permissions, compared to 9 today.

Prepare to invite users after go-live:

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal
  • Know the permission level each user will need to have

 

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work.

 

We will share more information during trainings including role definitions, templates, and other guidance.

 

For questions, please email Provider Services or call 1-866-690-5585.

Aug 17, 2026
This is a reminder that the attending provider is
required

The attending provider is the individual who has overall responsibility for the patient’s medical care and treatment reported in the claim/encounter. The attending provider requirement includes all claim submission methods (paper, HealthPAS Online Portal, or 837I).
MaineCare continues to monitor claims for compliance with applicable billing requirements and to work collaboratively with individual providers and provider associations to address identified issues and provide guidance where needed. There is no information in the attending provider field, or the information is not valid.
Providers are submitting a Type 2 NPI instead of a Type 1 NPI. Providers must use a Type 1 NPI unless self-referred screening mammography is the only service billed on the claim.

About 8% of all babies in Maine were born substance-exposed—that's three each day. The life-saving drug Naloxone was not generally available. There were few treatment beds, and when someone was ready to get into recovery, even fewer treatment options were available if they didn't have health insurance.

When I took office, I knew that what Maine had been doing for so many years just wasn't working. We needed a coordinated response that broke down the silos of government, set aside the stigma, and spoke out about every aspect of the opioid epidemic. I promised that we would put the full force of my Administration behind the families who lost loved ones, the businesses who lost employees, and all the communities that have been diminished by this public health crisis. 

So my first executive order, signed on my first day in office, fulfilled the will of the people of Maine and expanded MaineCare to more than 90,000 people. Today, nearly 40,000 people receive treatment for substance use disorder through MaineCare. Expanding health insurance was a critical first step to confronting the opioid crisis.

I named Gordon Smith as my Director of Opioid Response, and I signed the second executive order with basic strategies and specific action steps. That order established a Prevention and Recovery Cabinet made up of commissioners from 14 government agencies and the Attorney General's Office and the Judicial Branch.

We outlined key steps to preventing overdoses and deaths, including making Naloxone widely available statewide, and since early 2019, we've distributed more than 870,000 doses of Naloxone, which has saved thousands of lives.

We then outlined steps to expand effective treatment and recovery measures, including training 250 recovery coaches and funding recovery coaches in ten emergency departments. Now we've trained more than 4,000 individuals as recovery coaches, and we've increased the number of certified recovery residences from 11 to 119.

We've created youth recovery coaching programs in Hancock and Washington counties in the schools, creating peer-to-peer connections that can give a young person the hope to face the future. And we held statewide trainings and leadership conferences, which taught more than 400 youth how to create positive change in their communities. 

We created TreatmentConnection.com, a one-stop-shop for individuals seeking treatment that allows them to find out in real time what there is available for behavioral health services among more than 500 providers. Since that went live in 2025, TreatmentConnection has been used 8,000 times.

We're also increasing good-paying jobs for people in recovery, rewarding businesses who understand the unique experiences of people in recovery. And we've created the Recovery Friendly Workplaces designation, a certification held by 86 businesses who employ nearly 25,000 people statewide.

You know, we're not giving up on interdiction as well, making sure we take drugs off the street as much as possible to keep people from becoming addicted in the first place. My Administration is doing what we can in a responsible manner to stop deadly drugs from reaching Maine, to prevent substance abuse in the first place, to treat it when we can't prevent it, to set people on a lifelong path to recovery, and, above all else, to save lives.

From January to June of this year, fatal overdoses decreased by nearly 9% in Maine. This is the fourth consecutive year of declining overdose deaths. And that's welcome news, but we know we can't be complacent. Every overdose is a tragic and, I believe, preventable loss of a valued life. So let's all recommit to supporting people as they start, stumble, or resume their recovery, and to responding to new phases of the opioid epidemic to save lives.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You are invited to join a Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) briefing to learn about plans to implement federal changes to Medicaid (in Maine, MaineCare) eligibility that will go into effect on January 1, 2027.   

During this webinar, the DHHS Office for Family Independence (OFI) and Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) will provide an overview of upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility for Expansion Adults:

items.content_text: This final rule requires that a State Medicaid plan must provide that the Medicaid agency will not make payment under the plan for sex-rejecting procedures for children under 18, and prohibits the use of Federal Medicaid dollars to fund sex-rejecting procedures for individuals under the age of 18. In addition, this final rule requires that a separate State Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) plan must provide that the CHIP agency will not make payment under the plan for sex-rejecting procedures for children under 19, and prohibits the use of Federal CHIP dollars to fund sex-rejecting procedures for individuals under the age of 19. For Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries who are actively receiving cross-sex hormone therapy, State Medicaid and CHIP agencies may continue to claim Federal Financial Participation for those hormone therapy medications for a period of up to 6 months from the effective date of this final rule.

Title IV Postsecondary Institutions: Workforce Pell Program Application Now Open

MAINE- The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) - https://www.maine.gov/swb/board/index.shtml announced the launch of Maine's Workforce Pell Application - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/pages/workforce-pell , providing eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with an online process to seek approval to offer Workforce Pell-eligible programs.

The launch of the application follows the U.S. Department of Education's publication of the final Workforce Pell regulations - https://www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-issues-final-rule-create-new-workforce-pell-grant-program (effective July 20, 2026). Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers. Under Workforce Pell, states are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before approval by the U.S. Department of Education.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state," said Vaughan Woodruff, Chair, State Workforce Development Board. "The Maine Workforce Pell program makes it easier for individuals to access those opportunities, strengthening the futures of Maine workers and Maine's businesses."

On July 30, the SWDB approved the Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/final-workforce-pell-determination-policy-8.11.2026.pdf , establishing the state's process for identifying, reviewing, and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. Developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System, and University of Maine System, the policy is designed to align eligible programs with high-skill, high-wage, in-demand occupations; ensure quality outcomes for students; and provide a transparent and consistent process for institutions and learners.

"Workforce Pell is an important step toward building a stronger workforce and expanding opportunities for people to gain the skills they need to succeed," said Laura Fortman, Commissioner of the Maine Department of Labor. "By aligning short-term training with the skills Maine employers need, these programs will create pathways to good jobs and help businesses find qualified workers. The State Workforce Development Board's clear, transparent process will ensure training prepares people for in-demand careers while meeting the needs of Maine's economy."

Pharmacy Prior Authorization and Claims Denials: Enroll to Avoid Denials

Aug 13, 2026

As previously communicated, billing providers must include the National Provider Identifier (NPI) of an enrolled MaineCare practitioner who is ordering, prescribing, or referring on claims submitted to MaineCare. This is a federal requirement. In the next few months, MaineCare will begin to deny pharmacy PAs for prescriptions written by providers who are not enrolled with MaineCare, and will subsequently begin to deny Point of Sale pharmacy claims that do not have the NPI of an enrolled prescriber on the claim.

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access, training credit, and post-training evaluation access.

Aug 11, 2026

In cooperation with the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC), officials from U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Wildlife Services will distribute oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits this week. USDA Wildlife Services will distribute nearly 599,000 ORV baits in Aroostook County from August 12 through August 24.

The fall ORV bait distribution follows this past spring’s distribution and is in response to continued rabid raccoon detections in Aroostook County. The USDA’s Wildlife Services spreads ORV baits to reduce the spread of the raccoon rabies virus in Maine. The baits help limit the potential for human and domestic animal exposures to the rabies virus through contact with infected wild animals.

Crews will spread the bait by air in rural areas and by vehicle in more populated areas. Each bait is a fishmeal-coated cube or sachet about one to two inches in size. Although humans and pets cannot get rabies from contact with the bait, they should not touch or move them.

Studies show that ORV baits are safe in many species of animals, including domestic dogs and cats. While dogs may get upset stomachs if they eat a lot of bait, there are no known long-term health risks. If a person has skin contact with a bait cube or sachet, rinse the affected area with warm water and soap. For concerns about a person or pet touching or eating a bait, call the Maine CDC’s 24-hour line at 800-821-5821.

Since 2003, the USDA’s Wildlife Services has worked to halt the spread of raccoon rabies in northern Maine. They also collaborate with Canadian officials in New Brunswick and Quebec to reduce the presence of rabies across Maine and Canada. The ORV bait distribution program in Maine is part of a larger effort by the USDA’s Wildlife Services to prevent the westward spread of raccoon rabies. This effort creates a barrier along the Appalachian Mountains from the Canadian border to Alabama.

Rabies is a virus that infects the nervous system of humans and other mammals. It spreads mainly through a bite from an infected animal. Once symptoms develop, rabies is almost always fatal. Timely post-exposure treatment can prevent disease in people. Approximately 90 percent of reported animal rabies cases in the U.S. occur in wildlife. As of August 10, 2026, 28 animals tested positive for rabies this year in 12 counties across Maine. These animals include raccoons, skunks, foxes, bats, and a goat.

To help protect yourself and your pet against rabies:

  • Keep your pets and livestock up to date on rabies vaccinations.
  • Feed pets indoors.
  • Keep garbage cans or other sources of food tightly secured.
  • Do not feed, touch, or adopt wild animals. Be cautious of stray dogs and cats.
  • Do not move wildlife. This can spread rabies into new areas.
  • Wash bite or scratch wounds with soap and water for 10 to 15 minutes.

Who to contact:

  • If an animal bites or scratches you, contact a health care provider.
  • If an animal bites or scratches your pet, contact your veterinarian.
  • To report a dead or suspicious-acting animal in northern Maine, contact the USDA’s Wildlife Services. In other parts of Maine, contact the nearest Maine Regional Communications Dispatch Center.

For more information:

  • USDA Rabies webpage
  • Maine CDC Rabies webpage
  • USDA Wildlife Services: 1-866-487-3297
  • Maine CDC disease reporting & consultation line: 1-800-821-5821 (available 24/7)

Photo of bait types: The bottom two bait types in the photo are a fishmeal-coated sachet(bottom) and cube(middle) and are the only two used in this ORV bait drop in Maine.

items.title: Maine CDC: Childhood Vaccine Guidance Remains Unchanged Following Federal Action — Maine Department of Health and Human Services News
items.content_text:
Aug 11, 2026
Maine will continue to follow the guidance of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) on childhood vaccine recommendations, despite President Donald Trump’s executive order on childhood vaccinations, per the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC).
“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are playing politics with the lives of our nation’s children. Vaccines are safe and effective and save lives,”
said Governor Janet Mills.
“Maine will continue to follow the science and the facts, and our approach to vaccines remains unchanged by yesterday’s executive order.”
“Vaccines are our most effective defense against vaccine-preventable illnesses,”
said Dr. Puthiery Va, Director of the Maine CDC.
“In Maine, vaccines remain available at no cost to eligible children through the Maine CDC’s Immunization Program. Maine’s school and child care immunization requirements remain unchanged by federal actions to date.”
As the AAP has noted in their 8/10
statement
in response to this executive order:
“Vaccine recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics are tailored to the health of children living in the United States and are based on decades of research and systematic tracking of real-world experiences. Pediatricians recommend children receive certain vaccines at specific ages based on when children's immune systems will respond best and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases. Sometimes this means children will receive a single shot that protects against multiple diseases, or they may receive multiple vaccines at one visit.”
Beginning in 2021, Maine removed non-medical exemptions from the school and child care immunization requirements pursuant
Public Law 2019, Ch. 154
. That decision was upheld by a vote of 72.81 percent of Maine voters at the ballot box in 2020.

You're invited! Are you looking for a new career? Maybe you are transitioning from military service, or just looking for a change?

Maine's annual Hire-A-Vet Campaign is a statewide effort with the goal of at least 100 employers hiring at least 100 veterans and military family members during a 100-day period.

items.title: US Department of Labor finds urgent care employer failed to pay over $113K in owed wages to workers for required orientation, meetings, training — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
items.content_text: ATLANTA – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $113,199 in back wages after an investigation found a Richmond Hill urgent care facility failed to pay its workers for hours worked and retaliated against a worker for questioning its pay practices.An investigation by the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Premier Health Consultants LLC – operating as St. Joseph Candler Urgent Care – violated the Fair Labor Standards Act by paying straight time instead of time and one-half in overtime for all hours worked over 40 when employees were required to attend mandatory orientation, meetings, and training. The employer also required certain employees to work off the clock, resulting in unpaid overtime, and suspended a worker who questioned pay practices, all violations of the FLSA.Workers and employers can call the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they think they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) Clinical Eligibility Review and Billing Criteria for Section 45 and 46 Hospitals Update

Aug 10, 2026

Beginning September 1, 2026, IOP services delivered by hospitals enrolled under MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter II, Sections 45 and 46 will require clinical eligibility review and billing criteria in alignment with Medicare’s IOP services billing requirements.  

Effective for dates of service on, or after, September 1, 2026, hospitals delivering IOP services must: 

  1. Submit a clinical review request to Acentra Health before delivering services to determine a MaineCare member’s IOP service eligibility. Members determined to meet clinical eligibility criteria as defined in MBM, Chapter II, Section 65 will receive a Case ID number to authorize billing for the delivery of IOP services by Section 45 and 46 providers. 

  2. With clinical review approval, deliver IOP services in accordance with their hospital licensure and the requirements of MBM, Chapter II, Section 65.05-4.  

  3. Submit claims using the corresponding CPT/HCPCS codes or revenue codes for actual services delivered including modifier(s) as applicable. Condition Code 92 (CC 92) is required in Form Locator fields 18-24. 

  4. Retain the clinical review Case ID number in the member’s medical record. Because IOP services without a clinical review Case ID are not eligible for reimbursement, providers must maintain clinical review approval records for Program Integrity purposes. 

  5. Deliver services in accordance with Division of Licensing and Certification (DLC) requirements.   

Please note: This notice supersedes previous MaineCare Section 45 and 46 IOP billing instructions including, but not limited to, the June 14, 2023 and August 18, 2023 messages.  

Medicare’s claims criteria are outlined in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publication, including MLN 13496 – Billing Requirements for Intensive Outpatient Program Services with New Condition Code 92.

For questions regarding hospital licensure requirements for the delivery of IOP services, please reach out to Anna Blackwell, Associate Director of DLC: Medical Facilities Unit.  

For questions regarding IOP service and eligibility standards set forth in Section 65, or the billing requirements for providers enrolled under Sections 45 and 46, please contact Provider Relations Specialist Tiffany Norton.

items.content_html:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Well, you know, one of the lessons learned from the pandemic time was how dependent we are as a state and community on producers from other states and other countries for basic goods like food, textiles, and construction materials. It occurred to me that our growing season is too incredibly short for us to become as self-reliant as we should be.

And after the pandemic disrupted markets and caused food shortages nationwide, we realized it was very important to have locally grown, fresh food right here in Maine and help our local farmers. So I used federal funding through my Jobs and Recovery Plan to provide grants to farmers to buy equipment to meet that higher demand for locally grown food, and I began to look for other ways to extend our growing season here in Maine.

Well, one of the things you can do is to provide greenhouses to communities who are able to support them and help people of all ages learn how to grow their own food. I called on the Legislature to provide one-time funds through the state biennial budget to buy greenhouses for as many schools and communities as possible. That will strengthen our supply of local food and will teach kids and families to grow their own food and extend the growing season.

The Legislature funded that proposal, and I'm proud to announce that we're now awarding grants to communities across Maine to expand their local food production and education programs through durable shared-use greenhouses. These grants were awarded through a competitive process. The organizations applied for them, and they include the Alfond Youth and Community Center in Waterville, where they're going to install a greenhouse to expand local food production and youth education. 

The Healthy Island Project in Stonington will use a greenhouse to increase access to fresh, locally grown food. And the Portland Community Squash will install a greenhouse to send more fresh produce home to low-income families and teach Portland Public School students how to grow their own food. Limestone Community School will install a greenhouse to expand their outdoor science program and provide students with hands on learning in nutrition, agriculture, and environmental science. And they'll run a student-run farmers market—I think that's great.

Over the past eight years, my Administration has invested more than $60 million in Maine farms and local agriculture, supporting the purchase of locally grown food, helping farmers expand their operations and equipment, strengthening our food system, and keeping Maine's farming heritage thriving.

You know, my grandparents were potato farmers in Ashland. I hope they would be proud that their granddaughter insisted that the state budget include a small amount of money for community greenhouses across the state. Sort of like the Victory Gardens of World War II and decades past, places where people of all ages can learn something about nutrition and how to grow lettuce, peppers, and parsley; where the older folks can teach the younger folks about the value of homegrown tomatoes and cucumbers and such and talk with each other in community. Where they can feel the joy of growing their own healthy food and appreciate what their neighbors are doing and appreciate their own Maine roots, the way I appreciate mine.

Dave Mallett, one of my good friends, the singer who passed away last year, used to sing a very popular song: "Inch by inch, row by row. Gonna make this garden grow. All it takes is a rake and a hoe and a piece of fertile ground."

Well, we're going to have everybody singing those songs in Maine in honor of Dave Mallett, and in honor of our agricultural heritage and the state of Maine's ability to become independent and self-reliant by community greenhouses.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.
